artists.biography:
Neil Mullane Finn, OBE (born 27 May 1958) is a New Zealand recording artist. Along with his brother Tim Finn, he was the co-frontman for Split Enz and is now frontman for Crowded House. He has also recorded several successful solo albums and assembled diverse musicians for the 7 Worlds Collide projects.

Finn rose to prominence in the late 1970s after replacing singer songwriter Phil Judd in his brother Tim Finn's band Split Enz. With the group, Finn wrote the hits "One Step Ahead", "History Never Repeats", "I Got You" and "Message to My Girl", among others. Finn rose from prominence to international fame after Split Enz broke up in 1984. While his brother Tim Finn left for England, Neil was the founder of Crowded House with Split Enz's final drummer Paul Hester in 1985. The group achieved international success in 1987 when they released the single "Don't Dream It's Over" written by Neil.

He ended Crowded House in 1996 to embark upon what was to become a moderately successful solo career, and has released two albums with his brother Tim under the title the Finn Brothers. In 2006, following the death of Hester, Finn reformed Crowded House (adding Beck's former drummer Matt Sherrod) and released their first studio album in over 13 years, Time on Earth, and the band began a world tour. In 2010, Finn commenced another world tour with Crowded House in support of their 2010 release, Intriguer.

perplexity.description:
Dizzy Heights is Neil Finn's third solo album, released in February 2014, arriving thirteen years after his previous solo effort One Nil. The album showcases an expansive, textured sound that reflects Finn's continued evolution as a songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. Recorded across Finn's own Roundhead Studios in Auckland and producer Dave Fridmann's Tarbox Studios in upstate New York during 2013, the album features contributions from Finn's family, including his wife Sharon on bass and backing vocals, and sons Liam and Elroy on guitar, percussion, and drums respectively. This collaborative approach underscores the intimate, family-centered creative process behind the record.

Musically, Dizzy Heights blends pop and rock sensibilities with sophisticated production touches, drawing on Fridmann's distinctive studio expertise. The twelve-track collection demonstrates Finn's versatility across multiple instruments—guitar, keyboards, clarinet, and vibraphone—while maintaining the melodic sensibility that defined his work with Crowded House and his previous solo ventures. Songs like "What If..." showcase a poppy accessibility, while the album's overall sonic palette reflects the careful layering and textural depth characteristic of Fridmann's production style.

Commercially, Dizzy Heights had a modest chart performance, debuting at number 130 on the Billboard 200. The album was released through Lester Records and Kobalt, positioning it as an independent project that prioritized artistic vision over mainstream commercial appeal. While it did not achieve significant chart success, the album represents a significant marker in Finn's solo career, demonstrating his continued commitment to songwriting and studio experimentation following his work with various musical projects throughout the 2000s.
